title: FDA Review of Shelf-Life Extrapolation and Stability Statistics Under ICH Q1E
summary: How FDA reviewers apply ICH Q1E to stability regression, batch poolability, and shelf-life extrapolation in NDA and BLA reviews, with named examples.
body_markdown:
## How FDA reviewers evaluate shelf-life extrapolation and stability statistics under ICH Q1E


FDA quality and statistical reviewers apply ICH Q1E as a set of ceilings. They do not treat it as a formula that entitles a sponsor to a given expiry. Across NDA and BLA reviews, the same pattern shows up repeatedly. Reviewers rerun the sponsor's regression. They test batch poolability at the 0.25 level. They check whether accelerated or intermediate data show significant change. Then they cap the expiry at whatever extrapolation multiple Q1E allows for the storage condition and the data actually in hand. For biologics, reviewers rely more heavily on real-time data, and in at least one review the assessor said outright that FDA does not grant biologic shelf life on statistical modeling alone[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=178)[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=177) .


This article summarizes the ICH Q1E framework as reviewers apply it, then works through named examples from Drugs@FDA review documents.


### The Q1E framework reviewers apply


ICH Q1E treats extrapolation beyond long-term (real-time) data as conditional. It depends on the observed pattern of change, how well any model fits, and whether relevant supporting data exist. Because a trend cannot be checked beyond the observed period, an extrapolated shelf life should be verified with additional long-term data when they become available[324](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=324) .


The key limits reviewers cite:


Q1E element What the guidance says


Little or no change, room-temperature storage, no significant change at accelerated Extrapolation up to 2x the observed period, but not more than 12 months beyond it. Statistical analysis is normally unnecessary, but leaving it out should be justified[325](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=325)[326](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=326)


Change or variability present The same 2x / +12-month maximum can apply if the long-term data are amenable to statistical analysis and the proposal is backed by that analysis and relevant supporting data. Without the analysis, the limit is generally 1.5x, capped at 6 months beyond the observed period[327](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=327)


Nature of the limits These are upper bounds on a supported proposal, not an automatic entitlement to 2x[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=328)


Regression and confidence limits Linear regression is given as an example. Two-sided 95% confidence limits for the mean apply when there are upper and lower acceptance criteria. A one-sided 95% limit applies when there is a single upper or lower criterion[329](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=329)


Batch poolability ANCOVA tests for a common slope and a common time-zero intercept, each at a 0.25 significance level to offset the low power of typical stability studies[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=330)


Sequence of pooling tests Test slopes first. Different slopes preclude pooling. Common slopes with different intercepts allow a common-slope, separate-intercept model. If neither test rejects, batches can be combined[331](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=331)[332](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=332)


When pooling is unnecessary Poolability testing is generally unnecessary if each batch's individual estimate already supports the proposed period[333](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=333)


### Extrapolation decisions in NDA reviews


#### Extrapolation accepted when data and statistics align


- **OsmoPrep (NDA 021892).** Three validation batches per package type had 12 months at room temperature and 6 months at accelerated conditions, and the sponsor requested 24 months[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=27) . Analyses under ICH Q1E supported 24 months for the attributes with specification limits. The reviewer's independent checks closely matched the sponsor's results[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=28) .
- **Kyprolis (carfilzomib for injection, NDA 202714).** The sponsor proposed 18 months from 12 months of refrigerated long-term data[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=29) . FDA's statistical analysis estimated shelf lives longer than 18 months, and Q1E permitted the 6-month extrapolation for a refrigerated product[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=30) .
- **Mayzent (siponimod).** FDA granted 18 months at 2 to 8°C for tablets in HDPE bottles, finding the extrapolation consistent with ICH Q1E. It granted only 9 months for the blister titration pack because assay was predicted to decline faster in that configuration[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=145) . Different presentations of the same product can end up with different expiries when their degradation rates differ.


#### Significant change at accelerated or intermediate conditions blocks or limits extrapolation


The most common reason reviewers cut a proposed shelf life is significant change at accelerated (or intermediate) storage.


- **Veklury (remdesivir) solution (NDA 214787).** At one manufacturing site, two batches had 12 months of long-term data and a third had 9 months[37](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=37)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=38) . Assay and total degradation products showed significant trends at the accelerated condition within 6 months. FDA applied Q1E's no-extrapolation approach and found the long-term data supported 12 months, which the applicant accepted[39](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=39)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=38) .
- **Daptomycin for injection (NDA 217415).** The applicant sought 24 months with 12 months of long-term data[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=34) . An out-of-specification result at accelerated conditions counted as significant change, while intermediate data showed none. Under Q1E, that allowed extrapolation only to 18 months. The applicant then submitted 18-month data for all six batches, which made 24 months the extrapolation limit evaluated in the later review[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=35)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=36) .
- **Bunavail (buprenorphine/naloxone).** Significant change in an impurity at both accelerated and intermediate conditions barred extrapolation beyond the 12-month observation for that attribute, and reviewers concluded 12 months was the permitted shelf life[257](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=257)[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=258) .
- **Treanda (bendamustine hydrochloride).** Significant change under accelerated conditions led FDA to reject extrapolation and base the refrigerated expiry on the available long-term data[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=146)[147](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=147)[148](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=148) .


#### The 12-month cap applies even when the statistics project far beyond it


Reviewers routinely separate the statistically estimated shelf life from the shelf life Q1E allows them to grant.


- **Soma (carisoprodol) 250 mg tablets.** The reviewer independently confirmed assay results projecting at least 60 months of stability and found dissolution also extended beyond 60 months[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=222)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=223) . Applying the extrapolation limit to 18 months of data, however, the reviewer supported 30 months against the applicant's request for 36 months[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=223)[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=224) .
- **Veklury (remdesivir) lyophilized product.** Three batches had 18 months of long-term data. FDA applied Q1E's 12-month maximum extrapolation and recommended 30 months[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=40)[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=41) .


#### Refrigerated products: the 6-month ceiling


For products stored below room temperature, reviewers consistently applied Q1E's tighter limit: where data allowed extrapolation at all, no more than 1.5x the observed period and no more than 6 months beyond it.


- **Omontys (peginesatide acetate).** FDA's independent analysis limited extrapolation to 18 months for certain strengths and presentations, noting refrigerated extrapolation could extend no more than 6 months beyond the long-term data. No shelf life could be set for the 3 mg single-dose vial because a primary batch was rejected and excluded[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=255)[253](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=253)[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=254) .
- **Exondys 51 (eteplirsen).** The FDA statistical reviewer found the sponsor's proposed duration unsupported and estimated 18 months for both the 2.0 mL and 10.0 mL fills. The reviewer cited the 6-month extrapolation limit beyond the shortest observed period for storage below room temperature and requested more stability data[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=256)[210](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=210)[214](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=214) .
- **Bendamustine hydrochloride injection.** Reviewers initially granted 18 months against a 24-month proposal and required real-time refrigerated data to support the full period. Once the additional data came in, 24 months could be granted[250](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=250)[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=251)[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=252) .


### Batch poolability: how reviewers apply the 0.25 test


Reviewers apply Q1E's ANCOVA sequence directly. When both slope and intercept tests pass at 0.25, they use a single pooled line. Otherwise, they keep batch-specific terms and base the shelf life on the limiting batch[105](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=105)[106](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=106) .


Product and attribute Poolability result Effect on shelf-life estimate


Epinephrine injection, assay Time-by-batch p = 0.9480 and batch p = 0.3901, both above 0.25. Slopes and intercepts pooled[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=107) The pooled line's 95% lower bound at 15 months was 93.43% of label claim, above the 90% limit, supporting 15 months[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=108)


Epinephrine injection, D-epinephrine Time-by-batch p = 0.7556 (common slope). Batch p = 0.0025 (separate intercepts)[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=109) Three batch-specific bounds were each assessed against the 9.5% upper limit and all supported 15 months[110](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=110)


Children's Allegra Slope p = 0.0284, so separate slopes and intercepts were used[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=111)[112](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=112)[113](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=113)[114](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=114) Batch estimates were 47, 34, and 30 months. The 30-month worst-case batch governed[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=115)


Prilosec OTC Intercept and slope p-values 0.5761 and 0.6105. All batches pooled[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=116)[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=117)[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=118)[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=119) Expiry was estimated from the pooled line[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=120)


Gleevec, HPLC assay Slope p = 0.173 (100 mg) and 0.130 (400 mg), both significant at 0.25. Three separate lines per strength[121](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=121) Two-sided 95% confidence bands for each batch line were used instead of a pooled line[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=122)


The Gleevec example shows how strict the 0.25 threshold is. Slope p-values of 0.13 to 0.17 would pass at a conventional 0.05 level, but they still forced batch-by-batch analysis.


### Independent statistical reanalysis by FDA


FDA reviewers often run their own stability regressions, sometimes using an FDA stability program to verify the sponsor's estimates. In Arthrotec, the reviewer used lower one-sided bounds for assays and upper bounds for degradation products[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=229) . Outcomes vary:


Product FDA finding Agreement with applicant


Esmolol hydrochloride in plastic containers pH limited the 20 mg/mL product to an estimated 20 months. Other attributes (osmolality, assay, free acid, total degradants) exceeded the proposed duration[215](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=215)[216](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=216) No for the 20 mg/mL strength, because of pH[216](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=216)


Omontys 70 ANCOVA-based estimates across attributes, strengths, and presentations. The shortest was 37 months, for HMW1 species in the 1 mg/0.5 mL syringe[217](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=217) Yes. All estimates exceeded the proposal[218](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=218)


Frova (frovatriptan) A common-slope, separate-intercept model for "other related" substances gave at least 72 months. A sensitivity analysis with substituted lower initial values gave 58 to 67 months[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=219) Yes. Both supported the 24-month request[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=219)


Etopophos preservative free Potency expiry was more than 84 months. The impurity's upper band had not crossed specification at 84 months[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=220) The conclusion agreed, but the reviewer rejected the applicant's statistical method[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=221)


Furoscix (furosemide) Analysis of upright and inverted assay data supported extension to 36 months[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=225)[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=226) Yes[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=227)[228](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=228)


Two patterns stand out. First, the attribute that limits shelf life is often not assay. Here it was pH for esmolol and an aggregate species for Omontys. Second, reviewers check the method as well as the answer. In Etopophos, they rejected the sponsor's approach even though both analyses reached the same conclusion[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=221) .


### Trending attributes and performance-critical tests


Reviewers look at which attribute is trending and whether it matters clinically before accepting an extrapolation.


- **Qinlock (ripretinib).** For a degradant that increased over time, the Q1E analysis used the batches with the steepest increases for extrapolation. Their predicted 18-month levels stayed within the proposed limit[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=70) .
- **Fenoglide (fenofibrate).** Dissolution decreased on stability, including at accelerated conditions. FDA cautioned that extrapolating beyond the long-term data might not be appropriate because dissolution was critical to product performance[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=71) .
- **Olysio (simeprevir).** An early decline in dissolution still supported 24 months, but the reviewer said the shelf life should not be extended without additional primary stability data[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=72) .
- **Rayaldee (calcifediol, NDA 208010).** Incomplete 12-month registration-batch data did not support the requested 24 months. FDA requested trend graphs and pointed the applicant to Q1E approaches for poolability and extrapolation[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=31)[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=73) . The reviewer accepted 24 months only after the applicant supplied 24-month data. That was approval on new real-time data, not acceptance of the original extrapolation[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=32)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=33) .
- **Arikayce Kit (amikacin).** With in-vitro release trending toward the specification limit, the sponsor accepted a 9-month refrigerated shelf life[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=153)[154](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=154) .


### Biologics: real-time data outweigh statistical projection


In BLA reviews, Q1E statistics play a supporting role. Real-time data on representative material carry the most weight.


- **Beovu (brolucizumab).** The reviewer agreed with the requested 18 months at 2 to 8°C, based on 18 months of long-term data from representative registration lots. A statistical assessment suggested longer dating was possible, but the assessor stated that FDA does not grant shelf life for biological molecules based on statistical modeling[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=176)[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=178)[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=177) .
- **Arzerra (ofatumumab).** FDA accepted 24 months for drug substance but supported only 12 months for drug product. Significant change in charge profile at 3 and 6 months under accelerated conditions meant those data could not be used to extrapolate under ICH Q1E. FDA also flagged declining potency in some lots and asked for tighter release controls[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=172)[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=173) .
- **Xgeva (denosumab) 70 mg/mL.** A Q1E regression of potency and purity kept the 95% confidence limits within acceptance criteria through 36 months. The reviewer also cited real-time data through 36 months, so the decision did not rest on projection alone[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=175)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=174) .
- **Avastin (bevacizumab).** The review recommended 18 months refrigerated and declined to extrapolate to the longer requested expiry because of substantial degradation under accelerated conditions[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=152) .
- **Voraxaze (glucarpidase).** FDA advised that biotechnology-product dating should rest on real-time, real-temperature data because protein degradation may not be linear[150](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=150)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=151) .
- **Keytruda (pembrolizumab).** In pre-BLA discussions, FDA said an initial shelf life beyond real-time coverage could be proposed, noting Q1E's statement that drug substance shelf life should be based on long-term data. Post-licensure extensions, however, should rest on real-time data from the approved protocol rather than further extrapolation[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=183) .
- **Arcalyst (rilonacept).** FDA declined to agree to a dating period before submission and said expiry and extrapolation would be decided on review of BLA data under ICH Q1 and Q5C[171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=171) .


Frozen products, including small molecules, get even less room. For Duopa (carbidopa/levodopa), FDA told the sponsor that no extrapolation would be used to set shelf life for a frozen product[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=149) .


### Post-approval expiry extension


Reviewers typically grant a conservative initial expiry and set out a route to extend it later. The regulatory reporting category depends on the type of evidence.


- **Bafiertam (monomethyl fumarate).** Future extensions based on statistical extrapolation require a prior-approval supplement. Extensions based on real-time data can go in a CBE-30[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=155) .
- **InnoPran XL (propranolol).** Extension through an annual report required full shelf-life data from three production-scale batches. Relying on pilot-scale primary batches would require a prior-approval supplement[291](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=291) .
- **Cequa (cyclosporine) and calcium gluconate in sodium chloride.** Extensions supported by data beyond the current expiry from production batches, or from protocol testing out to 36 months, could be reported in an annual report[292](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=292)[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=293)[294](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=294) .
- **Repatha (evolocumab).** A stability protocol approved with the BLA could allow annual-report extensions. For drug product, the protocol had to cover the full drug-device combination[295](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=295)[296](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=296) .
- **TissueBlue (brilliant blue G).** FDA granted 12 months despite limited data on newer batches and required any further extension to go through a prior-approval supplement[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=297) .


### Practical takeaways for stability submissions


Based on the reviews above:


1. **Expect an independent rerun.** FDA statisticians and CMC reviewers regularly repeat regression and ANCOVA analyses and identify the limiting attribute and batch[217](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=217)[216](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=216)[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=219) . Submit raw data in a form that allows this.
2. **Accelerated and intermediate data determine whether you can extrapolate.** Significant change at those conditions reduced or eliminated extrapolation in Veklury, daptomycin, Bunavail, Treanda, Arzerra, and Avastin[39](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=39)[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=35)[257](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=257)[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=146)[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=173)[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=152) .
3. **Projected expiry is not granted expiry.** Even when statistical estimates reach 60 to 84 months, the grant is capped at the Q1E multiple of real-time data[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=222)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=223)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=220) .
4. **Poolability at 0.25 is strict.** Batches that would pool at 0.05 may still need separate analysis, and the worst-case batch then sets the expiry[121](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=121)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=115) .
5. **For biologics, plan for real-time coverage of the proposed dating.** Statistical models support a biologic expiry but have not, on their own, been accepted as the basis for it, although FDA has let a sponsor propose initial dating beyond real-time coverage (Keytruda)[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=178)[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=175) .
6. **Agree on the extension pathway at approval.** The reporting category for future extensions depends on whether they rest on real-time data or extrapolation[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=155)[291](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=291)[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-reviewers-evaluate-shelf-life-extrapolation?showSourceNumber=183) .
